title: Thermodynamic and electrical transport properties of the half-Heusler plumbide TbAuPb
authors: Abhinav Agarwal, Snehashish Chatterjee, Maciej J. Winiarski, Orest Pavlosiuk, Dorota A. Kowalska, Piotr Wisniewski, Dariusz Kaczorowski
abstract: Structural, thermodynamic and electrical transport properties of TbAuPb were investigated on single crystals. The compound was found to crystallize with the cubic MgAgAs-type structure characteristic of half-Heusler materials. It orders antiferromagnetically at TN = 5 K and undergoes a transition into a different antiferromagnetic phase emerging in high magnetic fields. Electrical transport in TbAuPb exhibits a multiband character, with a predominance of hole-like carriers. Angular magnetoresistance evolves systematically with applied magnetic field and changes its symmetry near the spin-reorientation transition, highlighting strong coupling between the charge transport and the magnetic order. The results of first-principles calculations indicate that TbAuPb is a band inverted semimetal in the non-magnetic state, which becomes topologically trivial in the field-induced ferromagnetic state.
summary: This work investigates the coupled thermodynamic and electronic properties of the half-Heusler material TbAuPb. By combining single-crystal measurements with advanced DFT calculations, the authors demonstrate that transport properties are highly sensitive to the material's magnetic state. The findings suggest that TbAuPb is a semimetal whose topology can be tuned by external magnetic fields.
main_problem: The study investigates the interplay between magnetic ordering, electronic band topology, and charge transport properties in the half-Heusler plumbide TbAuPb.
main_result: TbAuPb exhibits semimetallic behavior whose magnetotransport properties are highly sensitive to its magnetic state. Theoretical calculations suggest it is a band inverted semimetal in the non-magnetic state, becoming topologically trivial upon field-induced ferromagnetism.
method: The research combines experimental measurements (magnetization, specific heat, resistivity, magnetoresistance) with first-principles electronic structure calculations using DFT/MBJGGA+U functionals.
model_or_system: The physical system is the single-crystal half-Heusler compound TbAuPb, which possesses a cubic MgAgAs-type structure and exhibits intrinsic magnetism due to partially filled 4f orbitals on Tb. The analysis covers both antiferromagnetic (AFM) and field-induced ferromagnetic (FM) magnetic phases.

main_assumptions: DFT calculations utilize GGA/MB-JGGA functionals with SOC included; the analysis models charge transport using a two-band model fit at high temperatures.

paper_structure: The paper systematically presents structural confirmation (XRD/EDX), followed by thermodynamic measurements ($C(T)$), then detailed magnetotransport studies ($ho(T)$, MR, AMR, Hall effect) across magnetic transitions, culminating in theoretical calculations of the electronic band structure and topological analysis.
why_interesting: The strong coupling observed between charge transport anomalies (e.g., $	ext{AMR}$ symmetry changes) and magnetic phase transitions provides a rich platform for studying emergent quantum phenomena driven by magnetic order, relevant to correlated electron physics.
